title: Al Bahar Towers — sun-tracking origami façade that halves cooling load
summary: Aedas Architects' 2008 Abu Dhabi towers wrap the glass in computer-controlled umbrella-like screens modeled on the mashrabiya lattice and on biomimicry (pupils, flowers). The panels unfold with the sun, cutting glare and glass heat and reportedly halving air-conditioning demand.
takeaways: Kinetic shading can be modeled on traditional passive devices like the mashrabiya.
Responsive façades target glass heat gain directly, the dominant load in hot climates.
Reported result: ~50% less AC demand and less artificial lighting.

title: Frei Otto — lightweight tensile structures found from soap bubbles
summary: Profile of German architect-engineer Frei Otto (1925-2015), Pritzker 2015 winner and founder of Stuttgart's Institute for Lightweight Structures. He form-found membrane and cable-net roofs from soap films, bird skulls and spider webs; works include the 1972 Munich Olympic Stadium and the 1967 Montreal Expo pavilion.
takeaways: Physical form-finding (soap films, hanging chains) yields minimal-material structures.
Study the Munich Olympic Stadium roof as the canonical cable-net example.
Otto's experiments are the ancestor of today's parametric architecture.

title: India ink wood staining — instant black picture frames without fumes
summary: An artist stains raw wood picture frames with India ink (Speedball) to get the thin black-metal-frame look. It dries almost instantly and, unlike stain, doesn't smell.
takeaways: India ink works as a quick, odorless black stain on wood frames.
Cheap way to get a gallery-style thin black frame for your own work.

title: Bubble cymatics — speaker-driven soap film patterns (with pseudoscience)
summary: A soap bubble mounted on a speaker under a ring light shows standing-wave cymatic patterns as frequencies change. The visual is real and easy to reproduce; the account wraps it in rife-frequency and '4D shape' healing claims you should ignore.
takeaways: A bubble plus a speaker and ring light is a cheap cymatics rig.
Health and '4D' claims in the caption are unsupported.

title: Victoriano 'Jumpman' — 29-frame hand-painted animated graffiti mural
summary: Graffiti artist Victoriano spray-painted 29 sequential frames of a Michael Jordan dunk over a few days in the studio and shot them as a stop-motion loop. A clean example of 'motion graffiti': each frame is a full mural, the animation is the edit.
takeaways: Frame-by-frame painting on one wall can be shot as stop-motion.
~29 frames is enough for a readable short loop of a single action.

title: 3D cymatic pattern — cross-sectioned in 3D software to form an image
summary: Reposted TikTok on cymatics (petri dish on a speaker under light) claiming someone built a 3D cymatic form in 3D software and colored cross-sections into an image. Mostly 'code of reality' mysticism with little explained technique.
takeaways: Cymatic patterns can be modeled in 3D and sliced for visuals.
Treat the 'code of the matrix' framing as hype.

title: Indonesian rumah adat sketches — black-and-white ink house studies
summary: A sketchbook series of traditional Indonesian vernacular houses (rumah adat) in black ink. Good reference for architectural sketching of roof forms and line weight.
takeaways: Reference for drawing vernacular roof forms in pure line.

title: Tien Dao drawings — reposted showcase of a standout illustrator
summary: A repost spotlighting drawing work by @tiendao06 with no process or commentary. Worth following the original artist; the post itself has no technique content.
takeaways: Follow @tiendao06 directly for the original work.

title: Thomas, West Virginia — 'A Walk from Moon Pool to Front Street'
summary: A single image by J.R. Brubaker titled 'A Walk from Moon Pool to Front Street', Thomas, WV, dated 12/29/20. No medium or process given; mood reference only.
takeaways: Mood reference for small-town Appalachian scenes.

title: Jenny Vyas 'REPOSE' — Women's History Month mural at Soho House Chicago
summary: Muralist Jenny Vyas painted 'REPOSE' on the corners of Soho House Chicago with Artist Replete, invited by Threadless and Careful. Reference for large-scale figurative mural work in a commercial setting.
takeaways: Brand-sponsored corner murals are a route for artist commissions.

title: Cascadia oil study — small 9x12 forest landscape on canvas
summary: A 9 x 12 inch oil-on-canvas Pacific Northwest forest piece from Cascadia Art Project. Mood and palette reference only.
takeaways: Small-format plein-air-style forest study, palette reference.

title: Decalcomania — surrealist paint-transfer for chance-driven portraits
summary: The artist explains decalcomania, Oscar Domínguez's surrealist method of pressing paint between surfaces to transfer random textures. They start with a rough portrait silhouette, let the transfer create the texture, then commit to it and pull form and dimension out of the splotches.
takeaways: Press-and-lift paint transfer gives unrepeatable organic textures.
Start with a loose silhouette so chance has a direction.
Commit to the accident and render form out of what's already there.

title: Kadlab logo build — Illustrator logo construction showcase
summary: A repost of a logo design by @kadlab with no narration, padded with a logo-for-hire promo. Useful only as a visual of geometric logo construction.
takeaways: Visual reference for geometric logo construction; no tutorial content.

title: 'Mirror' by Brian Hyppolite — motivational rap over Paul Kenton artwork
summary: A promo for Brian Hyppolite's self-belief anthem 'Mirror', set to artwork by Paul Kenton. Pure song promotion with law-of-attraction lyrics.
takeaways: Song promo; little to study beyond the pairing of art and track.

title: Moritz Berg 'The Subtle Prompter' — minimalist ink-on-paper piece
summary: A 2019 ink-on-paper work (42 x 30 cm) by Moritz Berg from his diploma thesis 'Supposed Trivia' at the University of Stuttgart's art institute. Wabi-sabi minimal abstraction, shown framed in an interior.
takeaways: Reference for minimal ink abstraction in interior styling.

title: Three Capes Cabin — small cabin build shown as a timelapse
summary: A silent build montage of a small cabin from Three Capes Cabin, captioned 'as easy as one two three'. Inspiration for a self-built getaway, no plans or specs.
takeaways: Inspiration only; no plans, materials or costs given.

title: Every corner in 6 seconds — a year of street corners on Fujifilm X-T4
summary: A photographer cut a year of corner shots from a Fujifilm X-T4 into a six-second rapid montage. A simple series concept: one recurring subject, many locations, fast edit.
takeaways: Pick one recurring subject for a year-long series.
Rapid-cut montages turn a series into a short reel.

title: Google and Amazon profits — half came from marking up Anthropic stakes
summary: On the earnings night where four megacaps spent ~$130B on AI in a quarter, Google ($20.7B) and Amazon ($16B) booked roughly half their profit from revaluing existing Anthropic stakes. Meta, without that loop, only showed spending and lost ~$120B in market cap.
takeaways: Check how much of a 'beat' is non-operating investment gains.
Anthropic's valuation jumps feed directly into Google and Amazon EPS.
Same AI capex was rewarded or punished depending on stake exposure.

title: Oil curve back end — watch December CLZ26, not spot, alongside bond yields
summary: The trader argues the signal is the long end of the crude futures curve: compare spot /CL with December 2026 /CLZ26, which is breaking out toward $100, and ties that repricing to global bond yields rather than war headlines.
takeaways: Track deferred futures (e.g. CLZ26), not just front-month spot.
Back-month repricing signals a persistent shock, not a spike.
Cross-check with long bond yields.

title: Kronos — open foundation model that tokenizes candlesticks to forecast markets
summary: Walkthrough of Kronos, a free time-series foundation model from a Tsinghua PhD student that forecasts stocks and crypto. It tokenizes K-lines (OHLC plus volume) into discrete tokens and trains an autoregressive model on them, so it generalizes like an LLM over market data.
takeaways: Candles need a numeric-aware tokenizer, not word tokenization.
Kronos is open and pretrained, so you can fine-tune or backtest it directly.
Treat forecasts as a feature to validate, not a signal to trust.

title: Daniel Thrasher 'diagnosed artistic' — comedy sketch on creative life
summary: Musician-comedian Daniel Thrasher's sketch where a doctor diagnoses him as 'artistic': unmonetized hobbies, a thousand half-finished projects, being paid in exposure, hearing the AC hum in C sharp. Sharp, relatable satire of the creative brain.
takeaways: Funny mirror for starting too many projects and finishing few.

takeaways: Duplicate of the original sketch.

title: 'The Night We Met' — vocal cover by Social Repose
summary: Social Repose sings a short cover of Lord Huron's 'The Night We Met'. A brief vocal clip with little else to study.

title: 'Pompeii' — Social Repose vocal cover of Bastille
summary: Social Repose covers Bastille's 'Pompeii', keeping the chant-like verse in a stripped vocal arrangement. Useful as a reference for reworking an anthem intimately.
takeaways: Stripped vocal arrangement of a big chorus song.

title: 'Running Up That Hill' snippet — Social Repose vocal cover
summary: A few seconds of Social Repose singing the Kate Bush line 'And if I only could'. Too short to study.
